mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to edge up from their current depressed levels, commuter exposure will translate into more incidental shopping trips and higher RETAIL_REC within four weeks. The mechanism is that resumed workplace attendance restores weekday trip chaining into retail areas.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not rise from the current week and RETAIL_REC still falls further over the next 28 days, the commuting-to-retail mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in RESIDENTIAL from the current elevated level signals more time spent outside the home, which should lift retail visits first within one to two weeks and push RETAIL_REC upward over the next month.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below 13 and RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior four-week mean within 14 days, the home-time displacement mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below its recent narrow band indicates tightening mobility constraints or risk aversion, and retail activity will weaken within four weeks because fewer people can or will access shopping districts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 2 points below the t-0w mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remains about -58 to -60 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls more than 2 points below the current weekly mean and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 28 days, the access-restriction channel is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility rises sharply while GROCERY_PHARM stays roughly flat, discretionary out-of-home activity substitutes toward outdoor leisure and away from shopping centers, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the following one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM changes by less than 2 points
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week without a corresponding change in GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in WORKPLACES together with elevated RESIDENTIAL implies office-based routines remain disrupted, and that suppresses lunch, errand, and after-work shopping demand so RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains near -53 and RESIDENTIAL remains above 14 but RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days, the routine-disruption mechanism is not supported.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in PARKS mobility during late summer should precede stronger retail footfall because outdoor activity and shopping trips co-move in warm-weather periods, producing higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS has moved from -29.4 to -21.3 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to recover and RETAIL_REC still declines relative to the last four weeks, the seasonal co-movement hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES break above their current flat plateau, the joint easing of commute frictions should increase central-area shopping trips and lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks. The effect should be absent if only one of the two proxies improves.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -56 and WORKPLACES rises above -51
failure_condition: If either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES crosses the stated threshold alone and RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, the joint-access mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A further increase in GROCERY_PHARM relative to RETAIL_REC indicates substitution toward essential errands and away from discretionary shopping, so retail-and-recreation mobility will remain weaker over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while RETAIL_REC stays below -60
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises while RETAIL_REC remains near or above its current level for four consecutive weeks, the essential-errand substitution story is rejected.
